Okay, let me try to work through this problem step by step. The question is about finding the smallest integer p such that the sequence s₁, s₂, s₃, ... becomes periodic after some point with a period at most p. 

First, I need to understand what the sequence s_n represents. Each s_n is the sum of applying the function f n times to each element in the set S={1,2,...,20}. So s₁ is the sum of f(k) for k from 1 to 20, s₂ is the sum of f(f(k)) for each k, and so on.

Since f is a function from S to S, it's essentially a permutation of the set S. In permutations, elements form cycles. For example, if f(1)=2, f(2)=3, f(3)=1, then 1,2,3 form a cycle of length 3. The key here is that each element will eventually enter a cycle because the set is finite.

The sequence s_n depends on how these cycles behave. Each time we apply f, we're moving each element along its cycle. After some number of applications equal to the cycle length, the elements return to their starting points. So the sum s_n will start repeating once all elements have completed an integer number of cycles.

The period of the entire sequence s_n would be the least common multiple (LCM) of all the cycle lengths in the permutation induced by f. Since the set S has 20 elements, the possible cycle lengths are divisors of 20. The maximum possible LCM of divisors of 20 would be 20 itself, which occurs when there's a single cycle of length 20. Therefore, the smallest p that guarantees the period is at most p is 20.

I should check if there's any possibility of a larger period, but since 20 is the size of the set, any permutation's cycle structure can't have a cycle longer than 20. Hence, the LCM can't exceed 20. So p=20 is the correct answer.
